conflicts.description: Lake Desjardins existence/identity: oral history says McConnell donated 'Lake Desjardins' to the camp, but no lake by that name is documented at or near the site
values: J.W. McConnell donated Lake Desjardins to Camp Kanawana (oral history, src_oral_aronson)
The camp's three lakes are Lake Kanawana, Lake Wilson, and Round Lake — no Lake Desjardins (oral history f_0023; corroborated by YMCA official descriptions of 'three private lakes')
conflicts.notes: Phase 2 search (2026-06-11): no 'Lac Desjardins' found in any registry. Oral history follow-up (2026-06-12): informant states Lac Desjardins was the ORIGINAL name of the lake that became Lake Wilson — it was renamed after McConnell bought and donated it (f_1206). Phase 2 research (2026-06-13): Pagé family genealogy reveals Magloire Pagé fils married **Olivine Desjardins** in 1875 (f_1228). The Pagé family owned extensive land in Saint-Sauveur (lot 43, côte Saint-Elmire) and sold property to the YMCA c. 1910. If the lake sat on Pagé-Desjardins family land, 'Lac Desjardins' likely refers to Olivine's maiden name — a common Quebec toponymic pattern where lakes are named for landowner families. This provides a plausible genealogical origin for the name. Remaining: land registry confirmation linking specific Pagé parcels to the lake.
